+numeric values are always nonempty or categories are always known. A valid query
+may have missing numbers or unseen categories even when the visible sample has
+none. First make parsing and prediction defined for every declared column under
+those cases. Fit imputation statistics only on training rows; provide a stable
+fallback for all-missing columns and unknown categories. Keep finite-value behavior
+unchanged while fixing this input contract. Record that hypothesis and run normal
+five-fold validation once. Do not perform extra model fitting or a parameter sweep.
+Once the contract holds, continue with one controlled evidence-driven improvement.

task.description: Research a binary classifier using the provided visible training rows. Use the locked five-fold plan and generate valid query predictions.

failedAttempts.reason: Fixed Docker static network topology and controller runtime packaging; original C5 and request retained, previous failed attempt charged conservatively

claim.hypothesis: Cabin deck contains residual evacuation and socioeconomic information not captured by class, sex, title, and fare; adding a fold-local deck category should improve pooled five-fold accuracy without relying on query labels.
claim.intendedChange: Add one categorical deck feature derived from the first Cabin character, with missing cabins mapped to U, to the existing additive model; leave all prior features, weights, and group handling unchanged.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one improvement experiment: adding a fold-local Cabin deck feature produced pooled five-fold accuracy 0.7980, below the prior 0.7994 baseline, so selection retained the prior solution.
limitations: The experiment tested only the prespecified deck feature change; no external labels or network information were used.
The locked five-fold estimate has ordinary sampling uncertainty, and the deck signal was sparse with many missing Cabin values.

claim.hypothesis: Group outcomes are more predictive when stratified by passenger sex: mixed-sex ticket or surname groups can let male deaths obscure the stronger within-family signal for women and children.
claim.intendedChange: Replace the baseline's mixed-sex ticket and surname group tables with fold-local sex-stratified ticket and surname tables, leaving all additive feature weights unchanged.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one improvement experiment. Sex-stratified ticket and surname group evidence matched the current baseline at pooled five-fold accuracy 0.7994, so selection retained the prior solution.
limitations: The change was neutral on the locked folds and provides no evidence for query labels.
Only the prespecified five-fold pooled accuracy is used; no external evaluation was consulted.

claim.hypothesis: Missing ages are not random across title strata; replacing the blanket age 30 with title-conditional values should improve the child/young categorical signal while preserving the current additive and group model.
claim.intendedChange: Keep the current model and weights unchanged, but use title-conditional age defaults for missing Age (Master 5, Miss 21, Mrs 35, Mr/Rare 30) when deriving child/young/adult.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one improvement experiment: title-conditional imputation for missing Age produced pooled five-fold accuracy 0.7994, matching the current selected baseline, so selection retained the prior solution.
limitations: The change was evaluated only under the locked five-fold plan and ties the baseline; no external labels or network information were used.

claim.hypothesis: Adult women travelling with children or parents have a distinct survival pattern that is not fully captured by sex, title, age band, and family size; a fold-local mother indicator may correct these residual cases.
claim.intendedChange: Add one fold-local binary mother feature (female, age at least 18, Parch>0) to the existing additive categorical/group model with a small log-odds weight, leaving the locked folds and all other features unchanged.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one improvement experiment. Adding a fold-local mother indicator to the current additive categorical/group model achieved pooled five-fold accuracy 0.7980, below the selected prior solution at 0.7994; selection retained the prior solution.
limitations: The locked five-fold internal validation is the only evaluation used; no external labels or network information were used.
The mother definition relies on the existing Age and Parch fields and may miss or misclassify some family roles.

claim.hypothesis: Cabin availability, rather than the previously tested deck identity, may provide a residual within-class wealth and evacuation-access signal beyond sex, class, title, age, fare, and group evidence.
claim.intendedChange: Add one fold-local categorical cabin_known feature (known versus missing) with a modest additive log-odds weight; leave the existing preprocessing, group evidence, and locked validation plan unchanged.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one improvement experiment. Adding cabin-known versus cabin-missing as a fold-local feature achieved pooled five-fold accuracy 0.7980, below the selected baseline at 0.7994, so selection retained the prior solution.
limitations: Only the locked five-fold pooled accuracy was used; no external labels or network information were used.
The cabin-availability feature was tested with one fixed modest weight and was not selected.

failedAttempts.reason: Fixed Docker static network topology and controller runtime packaging; original C5 and request retained, previous failed attempt charged conservatively

claim.hypothesis: The surname component is a fragile sparse group signal: unlike the stronger fold-local demographic features and ticket groups, repeated surnames can mix unrelated households and vary sharply across folds. Removing surname evidence should improve pooled OOF generalization, especially in the lower-performing folds, while retaining all other components unchanged.
claim.intendedChange: Controlled ablation: remove surname collection and surname log-odds contribution; preserve the incumbent features, weights, ticket signal, smoothing, and locked five-fold plan.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment: ablated the fragile surname-group signal while keeping the incumbent model and ticket evidence fixed. Locked five-fold pooled accuracy improved from 0.79944 to 0.80084, and the ablated solution was selected for query predictions.
limitations: The gain is small and fold variation remains substantial.
Ticket-group evidence is still sparse and may be unstable for unseen tickets.

claim.hypothesis: The incumbent's ticket evidence may be overconfident for sparse, noisy groups; reducing its contribution while leaving demographic features and all other logic fixed should improve pooled five-fold generalization and robustness to unseen or heterogeneous groups.
claim.intendedChange: Changed only the ticket-group log-odds multiplier from 1.5 to 0.75; ticket groups still require at least two observed training members and all other features, smoothing, and validation settings remain unchanged.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment: halved the ticket-group evidence multiplier from 1.5 to 0.75 while keeping the model and locked five-fold plan fixed. It produced pooled accuracy 0.80084, equal to the incumbent, so selection retained the incumbent solution.
limitations: The change did not alter locked-fold predictions or accuracy, so ticket weighting remains unresolved.
Sparse and heterogeneous ticket groups may still be unstable, especially for unseen query groups.

claim.hypothesis: The incumbent ticket signal uses every ticket with at least two labeled members, so small heterogeneous pairs may inject noisy evidence. Requiring at least three labeled members should regularize this fragile group component and improve pooled five-fold generalization while leaving all demographic logic unchanged.
claim.intendedChange: Changed only the ticket-group activation threshold from len(g)>=2 to len(g)>=3; retained the incumbent features, smoothing, multiplier, and locked five-fold plan.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment: raised the ticket evidence activation threshold from two to three labeled members to regularize sparse heterogeneous pairs. Locked five-fold pooled accuracy was 0.80084, equal to the incumbent, so the selection policy retained the incumbent solution.
limitations: The threshold change produced no accuracy difference under the locked folds.
Ticket-group evidence remains sparse and may be unstable for unseen query groups.

claim.hypothesis: The weak fare-bin and embarkation components add noisy fold-local evidence beyond the stronger demographic and ticket signals; ablating both should improve generalization by reducing spurious additive contributions while preserving the incumbent's core model.
claim.intendedChange: Remove fare and embarked features and their weights from the incumbent, leaving all title, age, sex/class, family-size, and ticket-group logic unchanged.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment by ablating fare-bin and embarkation evidence. The locked five-fold pooled accuracy was 0.80084, equal to the incumbent, so selection retained the incumbent solution for query predictions.
limitations: The ablation showed no measurable accuracy change under the locked folds.
Ticket-group evidence remains sparse and may be unstable for unseen or heterogeneous groups.

claim.hypothesis: The weak family-size feature is a correlated proxy for household structure and may overfit fold-specific size distributions; removing only its additive contribution should improve generalization while retaining the stronger sex, class, title, interaction, and ticket signals.
claim.intendedChange: Set the family-size feature weight from 0.25 to 0.0, leaving all other feature construction, ticket evidence, preprocessing, and locked folds unchanged.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment: removed only the weak family-size contribution from the incumbent additive model. Locked five-fold pooled accuracy decreased to 0.79804 from the incumbent 0.80084, so the selection policy retained the incumbent solution for query predictions.
limitations: The family-size ablation was evaluated once under the locked folds and was negative.
Fold variation remains substantial, and sparse ticket evidence may still be unstable for unseen groups.

task.description: Research a binary classifier using the provided visible training rows. Use the locked five-fold plan and generate valid query predictions.

claim.hypothesis: Ticket-group proportions are unstable for small heterogeneous groups; stronger fixed Laplace smoothing toward the global midpoint should reduce overconfident sparse ticket evidence and improve locked-fold generalization while preserving all demographic components.
claim.intendedChange: Change only ticket-group smoothing from (sum+1)/(n+2) to (sum+2)/(n+4), leaving features, weights, activation threshold, folds, and output format unchanged.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment: stronger fixed Laplace smoothing of ticket-group evidence produced pooled five-fold accuracy 0.79944, below the incumbent 0.80084, so the selection policy retained the incumbent solution for query predictions.
limitations: The change was evaluated only under the locked five-fold plan; no external labels or network information were used.
Ticket-group evidence remains potentially unstable for sparse or unseen groups, and fold variation remains substantial.

claim.hypothesis: The incumbent's ticket multiplier can still let small, highly imbalanced groups overwhelm the stronger demographic evidence; clipping the fold-local ticket log-odds before applying the fixed multiplier should regularize sparse group outliers and improve generalization to unseen or heterogeneous query tickets.
claim.intendedChange: Keep every feature, weight, smoothing rule, and split fixed; clip only the ticket-group log-odds contribution to [-1,1] before the existing 1.5 multiplier.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled improvement experiment: clipping ticket-group log-odds to [-1,1] before the fixed multiplier produced pooled five-fold accuracy 0.80084, matching the incumbent. The selection policy retained the incumbent solution for query predictions.
limitations: The change was evaluated only under the locked five-fold plan; no external labels or network information were used.
The tie leaves sparse ticket-group stability unresolved, and fold variation remains substantial.

claim.hypothesis: The title-by-class interaction is a redundant, sparse refinement of the stronger sex, title, class, and sex-by-class signals; removing this fragile correlated component may improve generalization across folds and to unseen passenger groups.
claim.intendedChange: Ablate only the titleclass additive evidence by setting its fixed weight from 0.8 to 0.0; keep every other feature, ticket evidence rule, smoothing, and prediction threshold unchanged.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment: ablating the title-by-class interaction reduced locked pooled five-fold accuracy to 0.79663, below the incumbent 0.80084. The selection policy retained the incumbent solution for query predictions.
limitations: The result was evaluated only under the locked five-fold plan; no external labels or network information were used.
The ablation tests one fixed change and does not resolve remaining fold variation or sparse ticket-group stability.

claim.hypothesis: The title-by-class interaction was harmful when removed entirely, but its sparse correlated evidence may still be over-weighted relative to the stronger sex, class, and sex-by-class terms. Shrinking only its multiplier from 0.8 to 0.4 should preserve useful signal while reducing fold-specific overconfidence and improve generalization to unseen groups.
claim.intendedChange: Keep the incumbent feature construction, ticket evidence, smoothing, and all weights fixed; change only the titleclass additive weight from 0.8 to 0.4.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment: shrinking the title-by-class interaction weight from 0.8 to 0.4 reduced pooled locked five-fold accuracy to 0.79804, below the incumbent 0.80084. Selection retained the incumbent solution for query predictions.
limitations: The result uses only the locked five-fold internal validation and no external labels or network information.
The shrinkage was tested at one prespecified value; remaining fold variation and sparse ticket-group stability are unresolved.

claim.hypothesis: The incumbent ticket multiplier of 1.5 may over-amplify noisy small groups relative to the stronger demographic terms; reducing it to 1.0 should regularize sparse ticket evidence while preserving the rest of the model and improve generalization to unseen or heterogeneous groups.
claim.intendedChange: Change only the ticket-group log-odds multiplier from 1.5 to 1.0; keep all features, smoothing, thresholds, and locked folds unchanged.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled improvement experiment: reduced the ticket-group log-odds multiplier from 1.5 to 1.0. Locked five-fold pooled accuracy was 0.79944, below the incumbent 0.80084, so selection retained the incumbent solution for query predictions.
limitations: The change was evaluated only under the locked five-fold plan; no external labels or network information were used.
Sparse ticket-group evidence and fold variation remain unresolved.

task.description: Research a binary classifier using the provided visible training rows. Use the locked five-fold plan and generate valid query predictions.

claim.hypothesis: Within-ticket outcomes are confounded by mixed-sex groups; stratifying the existing ticket evidence by passenger sex should prevent male deaths from obscuring the stronger within-family signal for women and children and improve generalization to unseen groups. Numeric parsing was also made total for declared columns, with training-only behavior unchanged on finite values.
claim.intendedChange: Keep the incumbent additive demographic model and ticket multiplier fixed, but key ticket-group evidence by (Ticket, Sex) rather than Ticket alone; add safe fallbacks for missing or malformed Age, Fare, SibSp, and Parch inputs.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment. Sex-stratified ticket evidence, with total numeric parsing for missing or malformed declared numeric inputs, achieved pooled locked five-fold accuracy 0.80084. This matched the incumbent, and the selection policy selected the evaluated solution for query predictions.
limitations: The result ties the incumbent, so the ticket stratification provides no measured accuracy gain under the locked folds.
Fold variation and sparse or unseen ticket groups remain unresolved; no external labels or network information were used.

claim.hypothesis: Embarked is a weak, correlated additive signal after sex, class, title, fare, and group evidence; removing only its contribution should reduce fold-specific noise and improve generalization across the observed fold variation and unseen groups.
claim.intendedChange: Keep the incumbent feature extraction, smoothing, weights, ticket evidence, and total numeric parsing unchanged, but omit the Embarked term from the prediction weights.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment: ablated only the Embarked additive contribution while preserving the incumbent model, fold-local fitting behavior, ticket evidence, and robust numeric parsing. The locked five-fold pooled accuracy was 0.80084, tying the incumbent; selection retained the evaluated solution for query predictions.
limitations: The Embarked ablation was neutral under the locked five-fold plan, so its standalone value remains unresolved.
Fold variation and sparse or unseen ticket-group stability remain limitations; no external labels or network information were used.

claim.hypothesis: Fare is largely a correlated proxy for passenger class in this incumbent additive model, and its sparse fare bins may add fold-specific noise after class, sex, title, and group evidence. Omitting only the fare contribution should regularize predictions for heterogeneous or unseen groups while preserving the stronger components.
claim.intendedChange: Read and preserve the incumbent model, then set only the fare-bin weight to zero; keep robust parsing, fold-local fitting, all other feature weights, and ticket evidence unchanged.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled improvement experiment: removed only the fare-bin additive contribution from the incumbent while preserving all parsing, fold-local fitting, demographic terms, and ticket evidence. Locked five-fold pooled accuracy was 0.80084, tying the incumbent, and the selection policy selected the evaluated solution for query predictions.
limitations: The fare ablation was neutral under the locked five-fold plan; fare's standalone value remains unresolved.
Fold variation and sparse or unseen ticket-group stability remain limitations; no external labels or network information were used.

claim.hypothesis: Missing ages are not random across title strata; title-conditional fallback ages should improve the child/young signal for missing-age passengers while leaving all finite-age behavior and the incumbent additive/group model unchanged.
claim.intendedChange: In feats(), derive title before age and replace the single missing-age fallback of 30.0 with title-specific defaults (Master 6, Miss 22, Mrs 35, Mr 30, otherwise 30); all other features, weights, smoothing, and ticket evidence remain fixed.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment: title-conditional missing-age fallbacks produced pooled locked five-fold accuracy 0.79804, below the incumbent 0.80084. Selection retained the incumbent solution and its query predictions.
limitations: The result uses only the locked five-fold internal validation; no external labels or network information were used.
Missing-age imputation and remaining fold variation are unresolved, with sparse ticket evidence still potentially unstable for unseen groups.

claim.hypothesis: The incumbent sex-stratified ticket evidence still activates on groups of only two or three labeled passengers, where heterogeneous outcomes can create unstable high-leverage corrections across folds. Raising the activation threshold to four labeled members should regularize this sparse group component and improve generalization while leaving the demographic model and ticket multiplier unchanged.
claim.intendedChange: Change only the ticket-group evidence gate from len(g)>=2 to len(g)>=4; preserve all feature extraction, smoothing, weights, and prediction logic.

interpretation.conclusion: Completed exactly one controlled experiment: raising the sex-stratified ticket evidence threshold from two to four labeled members produced pooled locked five-fold accuracy of 0.80084, matching the incumbent. The selection policy selected the evaluated solution for query predictions.
limitations: The threshold change was neutral under the locked five-fold plan; sparse ticket-group stability and fold variation remain unresolved.
No external labels or network information were used.
